methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Arc Boats is a Series B transportation company founded by Mitch Lee and Ryan Cook that has raised $100M+ to date. The valuation universe consists of seven private frontier-tech peers in transportation, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Parallel Systems, and DeepDrive. No public comparables exist in a narrow peer set, limiting cross-sector triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a valuation of $190M, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $100M total raised proxy. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while three same-sector companies exist, none satisfy the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier clustering necessary to generate a meaningful narrow comp set. Drawing a median from the broader transportation universe would introduce excessive heterogeneity and is therefore excluded from the triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median point of $190M. This single-method result reflects limited comparable data; the primary uncertainty is the representativeness of the 1.9x multiplier for Arc's specific risk profile and growth trajectory. Additional data on peer financing step-ups or Arc's revenue and burn metrics would strengthen conviction in this range.
